text.p: Scania AB will reorganize its Latin American truck and bus manufacturing operation with a view to boosting sales in the region, a company spokesman said.

The spokesman said a new organization, to be named Scania Latin America, would be based in the Sao Paulo suburb of Sao Bernardo do Campo, and would coordinate the truck-maker's production in Brazil, Mexico and Argentina.

"Scania Latin America will help us integrate our operations and increase sales throughout the region, which represent 20 percent of our world sales," said the spokesman, who asked not to be identified.
He said the company's plans in Brazil included a project to produce the new 104 heavy truck model which would replace the 113 models.
"(The) 104 trucks are the new truck generation. We are importing the new technology and training staff to produce these trucks in 1997 in Brazil," he said.

The spokesman said Scania is Brazil's largest heavy truck manufacturer and controls 36 percent of the market. 1996 sales are expected to reach nearly $500 million this year, against $600 million last year, he added
